editorial:
You are stuck on a fancy train in the middle of a snowstorm when a rich man turns up dead. That is the setup for this stylish mystery, and it pulls you in right away. Kenneth Branagh plays Hercule Poirot, a detective with a famous mustache and a sharp mind. He has to figure out which of the passengers killed the tycoon. The train is full of big names like Johnny Depp, Michelle Pfeiffer, and Judi Dench, so every scene feels like a star showcase. The vibe is old-school glamour mixed with tension, and you feel like you are right there in the dining car.

The acting is strong across the board, and the costumes and sets look amazing. The pacing is slow at times, especially in the middle, but the final reveal makes it worth the wait. If you love classic whodunits, you will have a great time. It is best enjoyed on a big screen, so try streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting on Apple TV. You can also grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Poirot gathers everyone and reveals that all twelve passengers had a connection to the murdered man and his past crime. They all took part in the killing together, each stabbing him once. Poirot is torn between justice and mercy. In the end, he lets them go, telling the police it was an unknown outsider. You are left wondering if justice was truly served.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic whodunits and star-studded casts.
